name: Finale of Devastation
oracle_text: Search your library and/or graveyard for a creature card with mana value X or less and put it onto the battlefield. If you search your library this way, shuffle. If X is 10 or more, creatures you control get +X/+X and gain haste until end of turn.
blocked_sentences: Search your library and/or graveyard for a creature card with mana value X or less and put it onto the battlefield.
If you search your library this way, shuffle.

needs.what: a search whose pool is the union of two of your own zones -- your library and your graveyard -- from which one card total is chosen and moved. Wanted here as {"op": "search_zones", "player": "you", "zones": ["library", "graveyard"], "count": 1, "destination": "battlefield", "selector": {"types": ["Creature"], "mana_value": {"op": "<=", "value": {"x": true}}}}. The count is over the combined pool, so finding in one zone must exclude finding in the other.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `search_library` builds its pool from `ctx.state.players[pid].library` alone, and `return_from_graveyard` defaults its selector to `zone: graveyard`; running both in sequence is a different card, because each takes its own count and Finale would fetch up to two creatures instead of one. The selector language cannot merge the zones either: `resolve_pool` reads a single `zone` key and `validate_selector` explicitly rejects `zone` inside an `any_of` branch ("put 'zone' on the outer selector; a branch filters the pool it already chose"), so `any_of` unions descriptions, never zones. A `choose_mode` over a library mode and a graveyard mode gets the count right but is still not the printed line: "and/or" lets the player look through both zones before committing, while a mode choice is made blind and locks out the other zone.

needs.what: a way to make the shuffle conditional on whether the library was actually looked at during this resolution -- either an automatic part of the union-search op (shuffle iff the library half of the pool was examined) or a condition key that reads the choice the search just made
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `search_library` shuffles unconditionally unless `"shuffle": false` is set at authoring time, and the `shuffle` op is likewise static. `condition_keys` can ask about flags (`has_flag`, via `set_flag`), zones and comparisons, but nothing observes which zone a search decision touched, and `set_flag` cannot be attached to one branch of a choice the engine makes inside a single op.
